2:1.sourceText: Διὸ ἀναπολόγητος εἶ, ὦ ἄνθρωπε πᾶς ὁ κρίνων· ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίνεις τὸν ἕτερον, σεαυτὸν κατακρίνεις· τὰ γὰρ αὐτὰ πράσσεις ὁ κρίνων.
2:1.targetText: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.

groups.note: Greek you are inexcusable is rendered You ... have no excuse. The actual adjective and finite copula jointly express that predicate; the copula alone is not an independent lexical You.

The Greek vocative O every human is condensed to the second direct-address you. The whole actual addressing phrase is retained; this is a contextual pronominalization, not a claim that man lexically means you.

The Greek in-which relative circumstance is rendered on whatever grounds in the judging comparison. The complete case/preposition-relative construction supplies this contextual grounds expression without a separate Greek grounds noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB supplies an explicit object for the first general judging description; N1904 writes only the one judging there. Its actual later the other remains anchored in the following distinct judge-the-other clause.
